note: A finger permutation that sends fingers 2 and 3 one after the other, so each learns to move alone. The text is about fingers, so the tool leaves `show` out and the row under the tab starts on the fingers. The feel to reach starts "Practice until" and names muscle memory with what the hands will do. The tempo is moves (70 to 90 bpm), named only as a param.

exercise.title: Fingers 1, 3, 2, 4
exercise.why: Fingers 2 and 3 like to move together, so a pattern that sends them one after the other in the wrong order teaches each to move alone.

cells.text:
Press Play below to start the metronome at {{=bpm}}. The notes of the drill play with it, one note per beat, and the note playing is lit on the tab, so you can play along with it.
On each string, play the four frets with one finger each, in the order 1, 3, 2 and 4, then move to the next string as the tab shows. The row under the tab shows which finger plays each note.
Practice until the order is in your muscle memory: fingers 2 and 3 land one after the other, never together, without you thinking.
